findings_qualitative.value: Elevated HCN abundance rather than excitation is primarily responsible for high HCN/HCO+ ratios in AGN-important ULIRGs

evidence.quote: We interpret that elevated HCN abundance is primarily responsible for the high HCN-to-HCO [+] flux ratios in AGN-important ULIRGs.

findings_qualitative.value: Shock tracers are detected in many ULIRGs, suggesting ubiquitous shock activity

evidence.quote: Shock tracers are detected in many sources, suggesting ubiquitous shock activity in the nearby ULIRG population.

claims.hypothesis: AGN-containing ULIRGs have higher HCN/HCO+ flux ratios than starbursts at both J=4-3 and J=3-2
claims.experiment: Measured Gaussian-fit fluxes of HCN and HCO+ J=4-3 in eleven (U)LIRGs, compared with J=3-2
claims.result: Ratios elevated in AGN-important ULIRGs relative to NGC 1614, IRAS 12112+0305 SW, IRAS 13509+0442
claims.finding: Higher HCN/HCO+ ratio is a good AGN indicator at J=3-2 and J=4-3

evidence.quote: We confirmed that ULIRGs with infraredor (sub)millimeter-identified luminous obscured AGNs tend to show significantly higher HCN-toHCO [+] flux ratios at J=3–2 and J=4–3

claims.hypothesis: Excitation differences explain the higher HCN/HCO+ ratios in AGNs
claims.experiment: Compared HCN and HCO+ J=4-3/J=3-2 flux ratios
claims.result: HCO+ and HCN J=4-3/3-2 ratios not systematically different between starbursts and AGN-important ULIRGs

evidence.quote: Excitation has a limited effect for the different HCN-to-HCO [+] flux ratios between AGNs and starbursts.

claims.hypothesis: HCN abundance is higher than HCO+ and HNC in HCN-flux-enhanced AGN ULIRGs
claims.experiment: Isotopologue ratios HCN/H13CN vs HCO+/H13CO+ and HNC/HN13C at J=3-2
claims.result: HCN/H13CN ratios substantially smaller than HCO+/H13CO+ in three ULIRGs
claims.finding: HCN more opacity-attenuated, implying higher HCN abundance; intrinsic ratios separate AGN from starbursts more

evidence.quote: the observed HCN-to-H [13] CN flux ratios are substantially smaller than the HCO [+] -to-H [13] CO [+] flux ratios in IRAS 08572+3915, IRAS 12112+0305 NE, and IRAS 22491−1808.

claims.hypothesis: A molecular outflow exists in IRAS 15250+3609
claims.experiment: Analysis of HCO+ J=4-3 and J=3-2 absorption and redshifted emission sub-peak
claims.result: Blueshifted absorption at 5.4 sigma and redshifted sub-peak; outflow rate ~250-750 Msun/yr

evidence.quote: P Cygni profiles are detected in the HCO [+] J=4–3 and J=3–2 lines toward IRAS 15250+3609, with an estimated molecular outflow rate of ∼250–750 M ⊙ yr [−][1] .

claims.hypothesis: Double-peaked lines in IRAS 12112+0305 NE are due to self-absorption or rotation
claims.experiment: Compared profiles of lines of various opacity, moment-1 maps
claims.result: Self-absorption in smooth gas cannot explain all; moment 1 shows ~300 km/s velocity difference

evidence.loc: 5.4. Double-Peaked Emission Lines in IRAS 12112+0305 NE and IRAS 20414−1651
evidence.quote: The observed double-peaked emission line profiles of HCN J=4–3 and HCO [+] J=4–3 can largely be explained by rotation.

why_this_data.value: Multiple J-transitions are needed to disentangle excitation from abundance

evidence.quote: the excitation effects can be hardly disentangled from abundance effects, given only one J-transition.

why_this_method.value: Using molecules with comparable critical density minimizes ambiguity from differing spatial distributions

evidence.quote: using molecules with comparable critical density is recommended, because the differences in their spatial distributions are expected to be much smaller
